context: data_leg_206m_8b val printed 2.033 at both step 8000 and 8500 -- the first zero delta after five consecutive drops of 0.008 to 0.015, against a print precision of 0.0005.
why_not_yet_a_signal: a true improvement below 0.0005 prints as 0.000, so one flat point at 3 decimals is not distinguishable from a small real gain. The ruled criterion is non-increasing and it is not violated.
threshold: if step 9000 prints val >= 2.033 as well, that is two consecutive zero-or-positive deltas and the run gets investigated: check gnorm, lr schedule position, and whether warmdown 0.1 has begun. If step 9000 prints <= 2.032, the flat point was resolution and nothing is done.
registered_before: the step-9000 val line did not exist anywhere when this was written -- the run was at step 8720 and the last printed val was 8500. Unlike the b0-20 threshold (shape 149), this one is a real pre-registration.
outcome: RESOLVED 2026-09-03T10:0xZ: step 9000 printed val 2.023, a -0.010 delta, back in the normal band (the five preceding drops were 0.008-0.015). Threshold said <= 2.032 means it was print resolution and nothing is done. Nothing is done.
amendment: b0 read all 17 deltas: the step-4000 delta was +0.0060, already the same order as zero at 12x print precision, and the curve recovered to +0.0210 at 4500. So a small delta is not new. The THRESHOLD STANDS as a watch item -- two consecutive sub-0.0005 improvements means the curve has not moved at three decimals for 1000 steps, which is worth a look and is what was registered ('investigate', not 'stop'). What changes is the CRITERION it sits under, see criterion_change.
criterion_change: The ruled health criterion said 'val monotone'. Print precision is 0.0005, so any true delta in (-0.0005, +0.0005) prints as 0.000 and monotonicity is UNMEASURABLE once deltas fall below a thousandth. The run is now in that region. RULING (fb, from b0's reading): the gate becomes 'val shows no rise exceeding print precision', i.e. no delta of -0.001 or worse. That holds on all 17 points and is decidable. The flat-point threshold above is a separate watch, not a gate -- a gate must be decidable, a watch may be a prompt to look.

context: Arm A = today's layer-level hybrid at d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 attn_every=4 (9 KDA blocks + 3 MLA blocks). Arm B = head_mixed=3: BOTH mixers in EVERY block on a 3:1 KDA:MLA head split (KDA h=6 inner=768, MLA h=2 inner=256, latent unchanged at 256). Both mixers read the full residual and write it back; their outputs are summed, which equals concatenating and applying one o (o(concat(a,b)) == o1(a)+o2(b), verified max|diff| 1.43e-06). Question: does putting attention in every layer at 1/4 width beat concentrating it in every fourth layer at full width, at equal depth and near-equal parameters.
params: RECOMPUTED on 2bc3fe6f, not carried over. arm A 206,128,200; arm B 208,552,008; +2,423,808 = +1.18% of the model, +4.10% of mixer parameters. An earlier draft said -1.91%: that was computed for a layout where each mixer read only its own slice, and it does not survive the change to full-residual projections. THE SIGN FLIPPED. Mechanism: every arm-B block costs 5,134,086, which is BELOW arm A's KDA block (5,265,416) and ABOVE its MLA block (3,932,160), so 9 KDA blocks save 131,330 each and 3 MLA blocks pay 1,201,926 each. Arm B is larger because it gives all 12 blocks an MLA where arm A had 3.
what_params_buys_at_1b: what +-2% params buys at 1B: unmeasured; nearest point is Stage E arm 1, +26.46% params for +0.031 nat worse, not a slope
confound: DEPTH IS NOT THE CONFOUND -- both arms are L12, same ffn, same d. THE REAL CONFOUND IS ATTENTION COUNT: arm B has 12 attention paths of width 256, arm A has 3 of width 1024. Total attention width is 3072 vs 3072, equal by construction, but the COUNT and the PER-LAYER width both move together and this design cannot separate them. A result favouring B does not distinguish 'attention in every layer helps' from 'more, narrower attention heads help'. Separating them needs a third arm (e.g. attn_every=1 at full width, which is +8 blocks of MLA and a different parameter budget) and is not in this A/B.
threshold: Decided on val BPB at the shared token budget, both arms same seed, same data order, same cards-per-arm (2 each). Arm B WINS if val BPB is lower by more than 0.003 (6x the 0.0005 print precision, and larger than the 0.0021 arm-to-arm spread measured on the two doccu legs). Arm B LOSES if higher by more than 0.003. Between -0.003 and +0.003 is NO DIFFERENCE and the layer-level form stays, on the ordinary ground that the incumbent needs no reason and the challenger costs +1.18% params.
registered_before: No arm-B training step has been run at the time of writing. What HAS run: one forward+backward at B=2 T=4096 on card 5 (runs/audit_0904/b0_headmix_first_run.py, rc=0), which produced loss 10.603622, 232 parameters all with finite gradients, block0.kda max|grad| 2.374649e-04 and block0.mla max|grad| 1.304626e-03 (both halves learn, neither is decorative), 1,034 tok/s single-card no-DDP, peak 15.91 GiB. That is a smoke test of the path, not a measurement of the arm: no val number for either arm exists yet.
equivalence_gate: The inner= edit is held identical to the pre-edit code at bf16 resolution on both live shapes: d768L12h6 sha256 733d729d743a3e19 and d1024L12h8 sha256 84920c28d10664e7, unchanged across four separate post-edit runs. The gate is shown to discriminate by two FAILs (one weight ROW stepped one bf16 ulp: KDA qkv -> 3636b157b80502cf, MLA kv_down -> 6c7df168dea91216, both rc=1). Full record in runs/audit_0904/b0_headmix_gate_outputs.txt. Without those FAILs the PASS would mean nothing: the gate was adjusted five times before it first agreed.

amendment: 6e's two readings, verbatim in force. (1) READING RULE ON PARAMS: arm B costs +1.18% parameters (206,128,200 -> 208,552,008), and what +1.18% buys in val BPB at this scale is UNMEASURED, so a B advantage smaller than that unmeasured quantity is undecidable -- it cannot be attributed to the topology rather than to the extra parameters. The nearest point is Stage E arm 1: +26.46% params for +0.031 nat WORSE, which is a single point and not a slope, so it does not license interpolating down to 1.18%. (2) READING RULE ON THE CONFOUND: the design cannot separate attention count from per-layer width; a B win is read as 'this topology' and not as either mechanism. A third arm separating them is not scheduled.
criterion_change: The +-0.003 threshold stands as the DECISION rule (accepted by 6e, on doc_cu val BPB). What the amendment adds is the ATTRIBUTION rule layered on top: passing the threshold decides which topology to keep, it does not establish why. B better by more than 0.003 keeps arm B and is reported as 'this topology at these parameters', with the +1.18% stated in the same sentence and no mechanism claimed.
